thread:
maya: Heads-up — seeing FP8 enablement regressions on H100 when node temps spike. Kernel selector flips to slowpath and end-to-end throughput drops ~45%. Repro below, need quick triage.

jin: Oof. Any deterministic trigger? seq len / microbatching?

maya: Repro case: long-context chat workload, avg seq 2048, occasional 8k tails. Batch 1, continuous kv cache churn. Observed:
- cache_miss_rate ~ 0.28
- occupancy bursts -> kernel_muxer_v4 picking fallback kernels

alec: Can you paste the runtime log where it switches kernels? Also which TransformerEngine config?

maya: Snippet: 
```
[2026-03-12 14:23:01] runtime: profile window=120s: avg_latency=78ms, p99=410ms
[2026-03-12 14:23:01] kernel_muxer_v4: select -> fp8_fastpath (pref)
[2026-03-12 14:23:04] thermal: node_temp=83C, gpu_clock_drop=1
[2026-03-12 14:23:04] kernel_muxer_v4: heuristics -> fallthrough to fp8_safe_int8_mix (slowpath) reason=occupancy_surge
[2026-03-12 14:23:05] runtime: kv_cache_eviction spikes -> miss_ratio=0.31
```

rachel: That thermal event looks suspicious. L40S had similar earlier? Did you try pinning TransformerEngine to prefer specific aten kernels?

maya: Running with TE config: `transformer_engine: {preferred_kernels: [te_fp8_fused_bwd, te_fp8_fwd] , fallback_policy: auto}` — but the selector still swaps when occupancy crosses threshold.

sam: Quick checks: 1) run perf with nsys to see kernel durations around swap 2) try lowering max_concurrent_sequences heuristic to reduce occupancy 3) reproduce with synthetic kv churn.

bench-bot: perf run queued on bench-07: `./bench --model gpt-7b --prec fp8 --seq 4096 --batch 1 --kv-churn 0.3`

maya: Attached minimal nvprof excerpt I collected: 
```
GPU kernels (ms):
te_fp8_fwd         28.1
te_fp8_bwd         12.3
fp8_conv_fast       9.4
fp8_safe_int8_mix  64.9  <-- slowpath after swap
kv_lookup           3.1
```

alec: So the slowpath kernel is ~2.3x slower. Two axes: thermal-induced clock drop and kernel selection heuristic threshold that doesn't account for KV miss-rate. Heuristic currently uses occupancy + seq_len but not kv_miss.

jin: I'll push a quick patch to muxer: treat kv_miss_rate > 0.15 as signal to throttle max_concurrency and avoid trying to use the fastpath when occupancy is transient. Patch branch: `feature/kv-aware-mux`

ops-bot: CI triggered for feature/kv-aware-mux. Bench suite scheduled.

rachel: Also test INT8 fallback separately — FP8->INT8 conversion cost on H100 sometimes adds format-conversion overhead that + thermal clocks kills perf. We should measure conversion overhead and account for it in selection score.

sam: Agreed. Suggest scoring: score = alpha*latency_est + beta*conversion_cost + gamma*(1 - cache_hit). Tune alpha/beta/gamma via A/B on dedicated pool.

bench-bot: bench-07 run complete. Summary: baseline fp8_fastpath throughputs=3100 toks/s, after swap slowpath=1700 toks/s, kv_miss changed from 0.12 -> 0.29 around swap window.

maya: For next steps: 1) jin -> land kv-aware-mux feature branch with conservative thresholds 2) alec -> run conversion overhead microbench across H100 firmware versions 3) rachel/sam -> add kv_miss metric to per-route dashboard and alert at 0.18 4) ops -> schedule warmup ramps on nodes to avoid thermal spikes

jin: I'll open PR and include reproducer script and the nvprof excerpts.

alec: I'll correlate with driver versions (535.x vs 536.x) — saw slightly different clock behaviors.

maya: Thanks. If we can stop the kernel flip during transient occupancy spikes, should remove the perf regression for most workloads. :thumbsup:
